title: What if my gifts are just noise?
keyTakeaway: Speech without love is just noise — a clanging cymbal. Love is the more excellent way.
scriptureText: Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, but have not love, I have become sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.
keywords: speak love noise cymbal gong tongues angels gifts paul excellent way 1 corinthians 13
answer: Without love, even speaking in the languages of men and angels is just noise — a clanging cymbal.
why: Pastor Kincer explains Paul’s picture: a cymbal clanging by itself would drive you nuts in about 30 seconds. He says love is more important than both kinds of languages — men’s and angels’.

quotes.text: Though or if I speak with tongues of men and angels, but have not love, I am become a sounding brass or a clanging cymbal.
And if I had someone over there just clang the cymbals together, you know, in about 30 seconds, you would go, “You’re driving me nuts. What’s the point?”
There’s languages of men, like they spoke on the day of Pentecost. And there are languages of angels. But the key is love is more important than both of those.

title: Can I serve God and still miss knowing Him?
keyTakeaway: Being used by God is not the same as being known by Him; gifts without love still hear “I never knew you.”
scriptureText: Many will say to Me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in Your name, cast out demons in Your name, and done many wonders in Your name?’ And then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from Me, you who practice lawlessness!’
keywords: matthew 7:22 7:23 i never knew you gifts without love prophesy cast out demons mighty works known by god 1 corinthians 13:2
answer: Yes. You can be used by God — even prophesy and do mighty works in Jesus’ name — and still miss the most important thing: love.
why: Pastor Kincer points to Jesus’ warning about people who prophesied and cast out demons in His name, yet hear “I never knew you.” He says they were used by God but missed love, which he describes as obeying God.

quotes.text: See, love is to obey God. And he had the message, but he didn’t have the love.

See, they had faith to do all these things and these gifts and these spiritual manifestations were working in them. And Jesus said, “I will say to them, I never knew you.” Depart from me, you workers of iniquity.
You see, you didn’t have love. You might have been used of God to do things, but you missed the important thing, and that is love.

title: Does real love insist on its own way?
keyTakeaway: Love … does not seek its own, … thinks no evil.
scriptureText: Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
tags: love does not demand its own way
keywords: 1 corinthians 13:4 13:5 13:6 13:7 love patient kind own way record of wrongs not easily provoked biblical love
answer: No. Real love doesn’t demand its own way. It wants the right way — the truth.
why: Pastor Kincer walks through Paul’s description of love: patient, kind, not proud or rude. Love doesn’t demand its own way in the family, the church or the community, and it keeps no record of wrongs.

quotes.text: Love does not seek its own way. Well, it’s going to be my way. I’m going to hit the highway. You know, love doesn’t demand its own way in the family, in the church, or in the community. It demands the right way, the truth.
Love is not easily provoked. It, you know, they’re not touchy. You know, if you don’t say the right thing or do the right thing, they’re all ticked off. And love doesn’t do that.

title: Is God looking for fruit — or fireworks?
keyTakeaway: Character (love) comes before chasing spiritual fireworks.
scriptureText: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace… God is love. Love never fails.
keywords: galatians 5:22 fruit of the spirit love first 1 john 4:8 god is love manifestations character 1 corinthians 13:8 love never fails
answer: Fruit comes first. Love is the first fruit of the Spirit and the peak of God’s character, and you can’t have the manifestations of the Spirit without it.
why: Pastor Kincer notes that love is listed first among the fruit of the Spirit, that God is love, and that love sits at the top of sharing in the divine nature. His point: the fruit and character of God come before the manifestations.

quotes.text: Love, joy, peace. It’s the first fruit. 1 John 4:8 says, “God is love.” See, that is exactly what God is. He just gave us the description of God.

So the love is at the peak of divine character and it’s at the beginning of the fruits of the spirit. And believe me, Paul is telling us, you can’t have the manifestations of the spirit without the fruit and the divine character of God. That’s what he’s telling us. This is the way to get it.

title: Does “be perfect” mean never fail?
keyTakeaway: “Be perfect” means grow into maturity — not never mess up.
scriptureText: Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect. … that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing.
keywords: matthew 5:48 be perfect mature james 1:4 perfect entire lacking nothing spiritual maturity completeness hebrews 5:14
answer: No. Pastor Kincer says “be perfect” means spiritual maturity and completeness, not a life with no flaws.
why: Pastor Kincer says people hear “be perfect” and think it means never sinning. He points to Hebrews 5:14 and James 1:4 to show it is about growing up and being complete, lacking nothing.

quotes.text: “Be you therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect.” This is Jesus talking.
And they thought perfect was just living a life that had no flaws in it. No, it’s coming to what? Spiritual maturity, spiritual completeness.
Let patience have her perfect work, that you may be what? Perfect and entire, lacking what? Nothing.

title: What is the real goal of God’s Word?
keyTakeaway: Worship, prayer, and gifts are means — love from a pure heart is the goal.
scriptureText: Now the purpose of the commandment is love from a pure heart, from a good conscience, and from sincere faith.
keywords: 1 timothy 1:5 goal end commandment love pure heart good conscience sincere faith gifts means not destination
answer: Love from a pure heart. Paul says that is the goal of the commandment.
why: Pastor Kincer says “end” in this verse means goal. We tend to think the goal is eternal life or the gifts of the Spirit, he says, but it is love.

quotes.text: Now the end of the commandment is love out of a pure heart. The word end means the goal. You see the goal of the word of God is love out of a pure heart.
See, we think it’s eternal life. No, you’re going to live eternally no matter what.
We think that it’s the gifts of the spirit in our circles.
And it’s not. It’s love. And that’s why we have such phoniness in the spirit-filled world as we try to push something that God isn’t doing.

title: Do we want God’s blessings — or His rule?
keyTakeaway: We may want heaven and God’s blessings, but God wants to rule in our lives through His Scriptures.
scriptureText: They have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, that I should not reign over them. We will not have this man to reign over us.
keywords: 1 samuel 8:7 luke 19:14 gods blessings Gods rule rejected God rejected Jesus Bible obedience saving a nation Scriptures reign rule heaven approval
answer: God wants to rule our lives, not just bless them. Too many want heaven and His blessings without doing what He says.
why: Pastor Kincer says Israel rejected God and did what was right in their own eyes, and Jesus’ parable shows citizens refusing the king’s rule. People want God’s blessings and approval, he says, but God wants His Scriptures to rule their lives.

quotes.text: God said to Samuel, they have rejected me that I should not rule over them. They haven’t rejected you, Samuel. They rejected me.

See, the people didn’t want God telling them what to do. Is that America? Yeah, we want to go to heaven. You see, we want his blessings. We want him to prosper us, but we don’t want to do what he tells us to do.
People want God’s blessings and God’s approval. But God wants to rule in their life. He wants the Scriptures to rule in their life, and they don’t want it.

title: Do we only want to hear smooth things?
keyTakeaway: Pastor Kincer warns that people may pay ministers to preach what they want to hear, but Scripture is given to turn us toward righteousness.
scriptureText: Who say to the seers, “Do not see,” And to the prophets, “Do not prophesy to us right things; Speak to us smooth things, prophesy deceits.”
keywords: isaiah 30:10 smooth things false prophets bible truth preach truth righteousness saving a nation scriptures word church nation bible
answer: Many people do. They want to be told they’re okay, so they hire ministers to say what they want to hear instead of what is right.
why: Pastor Kincer cites Isaiah 30:10, “Speak to us smooth things.” He says Scripture is given for righteousness and good works, but people don’t want to hear what is right.

quotes.text: There’s many groups doing what’s right in their own eyes, hiring and appointing ministers to flatter them, to please them, not God, as it says in Isaiah 30:10, speak to us smooth things, speak to us deceit, don’t speak to us right things.
We don’t want to hear about good works, we don’t want to hear about what’s right, we want to hear that we’re okay.
And so they get the money, they get the big fancy houses, they get the cars, they get the fame, they pay ministers to preach what they want to hear.

title: What if a nation turns back to God?
keyTakeaway: God warns before judgment, and a nation that turns from evil can receive mercy instead of the destruction it was headed toward.
scriptureText: If that nation against whom I have spoken turns from its evil, I will relent of the disaster that I thought to bring upon it. But if they do not obey, I will utterly pluck up and destroy that nation, says the LORD.
keywords: jeremiah 18:8 jeremiah 12:17 repentance turn from evil god’s mercy bible morality saving a nation nations word church nation bible
answer: God says He will relent from the judgment He planned. Pastor Kincer adds that Bible morality is an umbrella of protection when God judges.
why: Jeremiah shows both sides: a nation that won’t obey is plucked up, but one that turns from its evil is spared. That is why, Pastor Kincer says, we need to get the Word out.

quotes.text: If they will not obey, I will utterly pluck them up and destroy that nation.
But, Jeremiah 18:8, if that nation I have pronounced destruction, turn from their evil ways, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.
You see, if we get them to embrace Bible morality, it is also an umbrella of protection when God judges.

title: Can the Word still turn a nation?
keyTakeaway: The Word itself convicts and convinces people; the turning of a nation starts with the church speaking Scripture beyond its walls.
scriptureText: So shall My word be that goes forth from My mouth; It shall not return to Me void, But it shall accomplish what I please, And it shall prosper in the thing for which I sent it.
keywords: isaiah 55:11 word of god turn a nation church preach the word conviction saving a nation scriptures word church nation bible
answer: Yes. Pastor Kincer says that if the church gets the message out, the Word does the work — it convicts and convinces people.
why: Pastor Kincer points to God’s promise that His word will not return void. He says it is the Word — not a denomination — that must get out, and the turning of a nation starts with the church.

quotes.text: But if we can get the message out, and the word will work. Remember the Bible says the word will not return what? Void — but it will be profitable into the purpose that I have purposed it.
But it’s the word. It’s not the Catholics. It’s not the Protestants. It’s not the Jews. It’s the word that’s got to get out.
You speak the word and the word convicts and convinces people. The word does it. You don’t have to force them.

title: Is church really boring?
keyTakeaway: Church felt boring when he refused to get involved; David was glad to go to the house of the Lord, and the church is the people who make it up.
scriptureText: I was glad when they said to me, “Let us go into the house of the LORD.”
keywords: psalm 122:1 house of the lord church worship getting involved desire for jesus division part 1 scriptures division unity church bible
answer: It can feel that way. Pastor Kincer says church was boring to him as a teenager because he wasn’t involved and had lost his desire for Jesus.
why: Pastor Kincer contrasts that with David, who was glad when they said, “Let us go into the house of the LORD.” Pastor Kincer says the church is made up of people, and the people determine what a church is.

quotes.text: When I was 17, 16, 18, church is boring because I didn’t get involved. I wanted to do my thing.
Or we just lost our desire for Jesus.
David said, I was glad when they said unto me, let us what? Go to the house of the Lord. Man, he was excited. It’s assembly time. Oh, glory, let’s go.
But the church is made up of who? People. And it’s the people that are the determination of a church.

title: Should church be as consistent as a Big Mac?
keyTakeaway: A Big Mac is identical everywhere; Paul says believers should speak the same thing, so the Holy Ghost, salvation and holy living should be preached the same in every church.
scriptureText: Now I plead with you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly joined together in the same mind and in the same judgment.
keywords: 1 corinthians 1:10 speak the same thing unity no divisions holy ghost salvation division part 1 scriptures division unity church bible
answer: In what is preached, yes. Pastor Kincer says the Holy Ghost, salvation, righteousness and holy living should be preached the same in every church.
why: Paul urged believers to speak the same thing, with no divisions. A Big Mac is identical in Brazil, Korea, China and every state, Pastor Kincer says — but in America church teaching isn’t, and that confuses everybody.

quotes.text: He says, I want you to all speak the same thing.
I can go to McDonald’s, order a Big Mac and it’s identical. They didn’t change the Big Mac.

See, the Holy Ghost shouldn’t be preached different in one church and in another way in another church. It should be the what? Same. Salvation should be what? The same. Righteousness and holy living should be what? The same.
Everything should be the same like McDonald’s is, but in America, do we have that? No! And so we confuse everybody.

title: Can a divided home still stand?
keyTakeaway: A husband and wife need to stand together in the same truth and moral standards, showing their children Jesus by example, or the home will not stand.
scriptureText: But Jesus knew their thoughts, and said to them: “Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and every city or house divided against itself will not stand.”
keywords: matthew 12:25 house divided marriage family unity children division part 1 scriptures division unity church bible
answer: No. Jesus said a house divided against itself will not stand.
why: Pastor Kincer says husband and wife need to stand together in the same truth and moral standards, showing their children Jesus by their lives. When they go different ways, conflict follows and the kids can’t wait to get out.

quotes.text: Jesus said these words. If they’re divided against themselves, they will not stand.

In the home, is it imperative that the husband and wife stand together with the same truth, the same moral standards? Is it important? And being an example to their children, not just telling their children about Jesus, but showing them in their life. Yes, it is. Why? Or the home isn’t going to stand.
Because the husband and wife go two different ways.

title: Who was really crucified for you?
keyTakeaway: No church name, group or famous minister can save; the focus belongs on Christ, who is one with the Father and the Scriptures.
scriptureText: Now I say this, that each of you says, “I am of Paul,” or “I am of Apollos,” or “I am of Cephas,” or “I am of Christ.” Is Christ divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
keywords: 1 corinthians 1:12 1 corinthians 1:13 is christ divided crucified for you unity follow christ division part 1 scriptures division unity church bible
answer: Christ was — not Paul, and not any church name, group or minister.
why: Corinth had four groups — “I am of Paul,” “of Apollos,” “of Cephas,” “of Christ.” Pastor Kincer says only the group focused on Christ is right, because only Christ can save — not a church name, group or minister.

quotes.text: You’ve got four groups here and only one is right. Can you rationally, reasonably, logically tell me which group is right? Yeah, the Christ group.
He says, was Paul baptized or crucified for you? See, was the Pope crucified for Catholics? Can the Pope save Catholics? No.
They’re focused on Christ who can do something. Not their church name, not their church group, not some minister.
It is Christ and the Scriptures.

title: Does God have grandchildren?
keyTakeaway: “My granddad was a Baptist, my dad was a Baptist, I’m a Baptist — don’t bug me.” Pastor Kincer says God has no grandchildren and no stepchildren, only children. Each of us has to be born again and meet Him for ourselves.
scriptureText: Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.
keywords: john 3:3 born again god has no grandchildren personal faith salvation division part 2 scriptures does god have grandchildren
answer: No. God has no grandchildren and no stepchildren — only children.
why: Pastor Kincer says you have to be born again yourself and have your own first contact with Him. You can’t use your parents, your church or your minister as an excuse on judgment day.

quotes.text: The problem in America is if my granddad was a Baptist and my dad was a Baptist and I’m a Baptist, don’t bug me.
God does not have grandchildren. He does not have stepchildren. He has children. In other words, you got to get born again by him. You got to have that initial first contact with him.
I can’t use my parents for an excuse on judgment day. I can’t use my church or the minister on judgment day because I’m accountable to find him and serve him and follow him.

title: Is God only for emergencies?
keyTakeaway: No. Pastor Kincer says God is not just for emergencies — we need Him every day of our life.
answer: No. Pastor Kincer says God is not just for emergencies — we need Him every day of our life.
why: He recalls that after 9/11 the churches filled with people praying, then emptied again in about 60 days, because people think God is only good for an immediate necessity. In the hospital, he says, he didn’t need a healer to come in — he needed the Healer, Jesus.

quotes.text: 9/11 came and the churches were filled with people praying. See, that’s how quickly God can change things. But did it last? No. 60 days. Churches were empty again.
They think God is only good for an immediate necessity. And that God will be there at the snap of their finger. And they are totally wrong. We need him every day of our life.
I don’t need a healer to come in here. I need the Healer. Jesus. I’m not panicked.

scriptureText: Give us this day our daily bread.
keywords: matthew 6:11 daily bread 9/11 need god every day prayer division part 2 scriptures is god only for emergencies
